text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:

- Nazi gold reserves of 337 tonnes confiscated by Allied Forces after the Second World War are presumed to have been divided amongst nine countries even up to this year, according to the French magazine "Le Nouvel Observateur". But this was already known.
- Petroleum sales in Switzerland rose by 3.5 percent to 8.285 million tonnes in the first nine months of the year.
- Du Pont Group, with European headquarters in Geneva, announced plan to modernise operations for $1 billion over the next five years and cut 900 jobs in Europe.
- Hotel and gastronomy group Moevenpick forecasts a profit of 18 million Swiss francs for 1996, a three million franc increase over last year's figure.

- The graphic industry's wage negotiations for 1997 fell through. Unions demanded increases of 2.3 percent, whereas employers wanted three percent salary cuts. A decision should be reached in court in December.
- Winterthur Insurance Group's Belgian subsidiary intends to take over the Josi Insurance Group in Belgium.
- Swiss tennis professional Jakob Hlasek announced on Thursday his decision to retire.
